items.t: Whonnock is a City of Maple Ridge neighbourhood and a board sub-area name in the rural east of the city, centred on Whonnock Lake.
Webster's Corners and Thornhill sit to the west and north-west, Ruskin to the east inside Maple Ridge, and the City of Mission lies across the eastern municipal boundary.
The east–west corridors are Lougheed Highway (Highway 7), Dewdney Trunk Road and 112 Avenue, with 272 Street and 280 Street running north–south.
The stock is rural residential and farm parcels, not urban subdivisions: the zoning schedule that governs most lots is the rural and agricultural end of Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019.
Minimum lot areas in that schedule are A-1 at 2.0 hectares, A-2 at 4.0 hectares, A-3 at 8.0 hectares, RS-2 at 0.4 hectares and RS-3 at 0.8 or 2.0 hectares depending on the zone text.
Whonnock Elementary at 27471 112 Avenue is the village anchor building, a Kindergarten to Grade 7 school in School District 42 (SD42).
Whonnock Lake Park at 27871 113 Avenue is the City's recreation site on the lake, listed by the City as a park and picnic ground.

Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) parcels carry the agricultural zone minimums above, and a subdivision of ALR land also needs Agricultural Land Commission approval — the City states that test when it reports on rural applications.
The same City report states the RS-3 minimum lot area is 0.8 hectares, so a 1.5-hectare RS-3 parcel cannot subdivide without rezoning.
A detached garden suite in the RS-3 zone may reach 7.5 metres in height under a 2021 zoning amendment the City cites in its rural application reports.

blocks.text: Whonnock: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Whonnock Elementary doubles as a polling place and community hall substitute — it hosted the Whonnock voting location for the October 17, 2026 municipal election.
There is no City recreation centre or library branch inside Whonnock; the Maple Ridge Leisure Centre at 11925 Haney Place and the library at 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road are in Town Centre to the west.
TransLink route 701 runs east on Dewdney Trunk Road, but most east trips end at 248 Street and only some weekday trips continue non-stop from Haney Place to Mission City Station.
There is no West Coast Express station in Whonnock; the nearest stations are Port Haney/Maple Meadows to the west and Mission City to the east.
The rural cost difference here is servicing: lots without community water fall under the larger RS-3 minimum, and well and septic work is a private cost rather than a City utility bill.
Maple Ridge utility charges are mostly billed on the annual property tax notice, with metered customers on quarterly bills — most Whonnock homes are not on that metered system.
Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) is the through route west to Town Centre and east to Mission, with Dewdney Trunk Road as the parallel local route.
Driving is the default here: SD42's bus eligibility distances (4 and 4.8 kilometres) exist because rural Whonnock addresses sit far from the school.
Check the wildfire permit map: Whonnock's forested lots fall under the same Wildfire Development Permit Area framework, requiring a permit or a covenant with wildfire construction standards.
Check Whonnock Creek and lake-edge setbacks: the floodplain bylaw designates land within its setbacks and land under 1.5 metres above a watercourse's natural boundary as floodplain.

Check the farm home plate and accessory-building limits before planning a shop: a City rural report shows variances being sought to deepen a farm home plate and raise accessory height, which signals how tight the default limits are.

faq.a: What is confirmed is the rural zoning pattern — RS-3's minimum rises to 2.0 hectares without community water in the bylaw summary — which is why buyers here budget for a septic inspection and a well potability and flow test on any acreage purchase.
Whonnock Elementary is the in-village school, at 27471 112 Avenue, Kindergarten to Grade 7.
faq.q: Which school do Whonnock children attend?

faq.a: Yes — Whonnock is one of the few Maple Ridge catchments with regular district busing. SD42 lists Whonnock Elementary among the schools with regular transportation, for Kindergarten to Grade 3 students living farther than 4 kilometres from the school and Grade 4 to 12 students farther than 4.8 kilometres, with registration deadlines each year.
faq.q: Is there a school bus in Whonnock?

faq.a: Only if the zone minimums and, on ALR land, the province's process both allow it. The bylaw schedule sets A-2 at 4.0 hectares and A-3 at 8.0 hectares, the City applies OCP policy discouraging agricultural subdivision, and ALR subdivision needs an Agricultural Land Commission application on top of any City rezoning.
faq.q: Can I subdivide a Whonnock acreage?
